title: Bird Feeder: code-generated pixel art in a free Windows preview — does it read well at desktop size?
author: birdfeedergame
selftext:
Posting from Bird Feeder's development account. Our earlier post here covered generated audio in the old build. This is the remake, with a different pixel-art pipeline and a free Windows 10/11 preview (v0.2.1): [https://verdiana-studio.itch.io/bird-feeder](https://verdiana-studio.itch.io/bird-feeder)

The concept and direction are human-led; AI agents generated the game's code, pixel art and text. In this remake, each bird sprite starts as a character map in Python, using one 48-colour palette and an integer pixel grid, then gets exported to PNG. There is no image model in that sprite pipeline. A linter checks palette and grid constraints. That makes individual pixels inspectable in code and catches technical inconsistencies, but it cannot tell us whether a bird's reaction feels warm or readable.

The size constraint matters: the garden is only 96 logical pixels tall, displayed at whole-number scale (192 pixels on a 1080p screen). The larger trailer close-ups help explain the interactions, but the everyday experience is the little strip. We'd especially appreciate feedback on whether clicking or stroking a bird produces a clear reaction at that actual size, and whether the movement stays comfortable while you're doing something else.

The preview lets you scatter food, pet visiting birds and fill a Bird Book, with seasons and weather changing the garden. Audio uses ElevenLabs and code synthesis; bird calls are interpretations, not field recordings. This is still in development, and we'd love feedback from trying it, including anything that is confusing or distracting. For other developers using code-defined sprites, what visual checks would you add beyond palette and grid validation?

The footage is the game's own rendering, staged with a prepared save and developer controls for visits, seasons and weather. Close-ups are enlarged; the bottom strip shows actual size on a 1080p screen. The opening desktop is a labelled mock-up. Trailer music is enabled; music defaults to off in the game.

Feedback here is welcome. If you'd also like to join the development community and discuss what you find, our optional Discord is [https://discord.gg/vCdUFcsYP7](https://discord.gg/vCdUFcsYP7)

replies.author: birdfeedergame
replies.body: Thanks! Would you keep a bird garden running while you work, or mainly open it when you want a short break?

comments.author: porchplant
comments.body: This is so cute! The strip does feel a bit small to me but I think part of that is because the bigger version looks so charming.

replies.author: birdfeedergame
replies.body: Thanks, that's useful feedback. At the strip size, are the birds' reactions hard to make out, or is it more that you'd enjoy watching a larger garden?
